papers.title: Biophysical Characterization of Interactions Between Human Salivary Proteins and Quinine
papers.abstract: Saliva is the first biological medium encountered by bitter compounds in the oral cavity, and salivary proteins have been indirectly implicated in bitterness perception. However, direct biophysical characterization of salivary protein-bitterant interactions has not been reported. This study investigated interactions between salivary proteins and the model bitterant quinine using complementary biophysical techniques. Pooled whole saliva (WS) from 44 healthy volunteers was separated into high- (HMW) and low-molecular-weight (LMW) fractions using a 3 kDa filter. Protein-quinine interactions were characterized by fluorescence spectroscopy, sedimentation velocity analytical ultracentrifugation (SV-AUC), and isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC). Fluorescence spectroscopy showed a concentration-dependent reduction in the apparent unbound quinine, reaching 59.28 ± 0.89% at 0.6 mg/mL protein in WS, with greater apparent binding in the LMW fraction than the HMW fraction. SV-AUC provided evidence of protein-quinine complex formation, with the LMW fraction exhibiting the clearest changes through the appearance of new, higher sedimentation coefficient species, suggesting quinine-induced multimerization. ITC revealed endothermic binding across all three saliva systems, with the LMW fraction exhibiting the greatest change in apparent binding enthalpy (∆H = 1.053 ± 0.009 kcal/ mol) compared with WS (∆H = 0.321 ± 0.548 kcal/ mol) and HMW fraction (∆H = 0.081 ± 0.158 kcal/ mol). These findings converge to demonstrate that human salivary proteins interact with quinine, with the LMW species (< 3 kDa) exhibiting the strongest apparent binding (17.53 ± 1.58% reduction in unbound quinine at 0.2 mg/mL protein from the fluorescence measurements). This work provides the first biophysical characterization of salivary protein-bitterant interactions and establishes a foundation for future investigations into the role of salivary proteins in bitterness perception. papers.title: Adipose-derived stem cell extracellular vesicles in diabetic microangiopathy: from pathological networks to clinical translation
papers.abstract: Diabetic microangiopathy (DMA) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in diabetes. Its pathogenesis involves interconnected processes, including metabolic disturbance, oxidative stress, inflammation, immune dysregulation, endothelial dysfunction, mitochondrial abnormalities, and impaired tissue repair. This complexity suggests that therapeutic strategies targeting individual pathways may be insufficient to address the multidimensional pathological processes underlying DMA. Adipose-derived stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles (ADSC-EVs) have emerged as potential cell-free therapeutic candidates whose multimolecular cargo may modulate multiple disease-relevant processes. Preclinical evidence suggests that ADSC-EVs can influence oxidative stress, inflammation, angiogenesis, immune responses, and tissue repair, providing a potential basis for multitarget modulation of pathological microenvironments. This review critically evaluates organ-specific evidence for ADSC-EVs in diabetic retinopathy, diabetic kidney disease, diabetic peripheral neuropathy, and diabetic chronic wounds, with particular attention to evidence specificity, therapeutic mechanisms, delivery barriers, and translational limitations. We further summarize advances in EV engineering, including parent-cell and cargo engineering, surface modification, biomaterial integration, and stimuli-responsive delivery, while distinguishing ADSC-EV-specific findings from evidence extrapolated from the broader EV field. Finally, we discuss major barriers to clinical translation, including manufacturing standardization, potency assessment, biodistribution, organ-specific delivery, long-term safety, and regulatory evaluation. Future studies integrating disease stratification, multi-omics, rational engineering, and standardized manufacturing may help determine whether the multitarget effects of ADSC-EVs can be translated into reproducible and clinically meaningful therapies for DMA.

Preclinical evidence suggests that ADSC-EVs can influence oxidative stress, inflammation, angiogenesis, immune responses, and tissue repair, providing a potential basis for multitarget modulation of pathological microenvironments. papers.title: Pediatric-friendly Smart Oro-solid Carbamazepine Dry Suspension (SOS-CDS): optimization, functionality and in-vivo taste determination
papers.journal: Bulletin of the National Research Centre/Bulletin of the National Research Center
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Pediatric formulations are challenging to design due to considerations of convenience. Many children are suffering from an epileptic condition at an early age. Continuing anti-epileptic treatment can influence bone metabolism in children. The research was undertaken to design a pediatric and industry approachable smart stable dosage form of carbamazepine (CBZ) supplemented with Vitamin D (Vit D). Methods Smart Oro-solid Carbamazepine Dry Suspension (SOS-CDS) was formulated using a liquorice-based suspending agent. DSC and FTIR were performed to observe interactions among CBZ, Vit D, and other excipients. Screening of various variables was performed using Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA), and the results were further optimized using a Central Composite Design (CCD) with two independent variables (suspending agent and mixing speed) and three dependent variables (sedimentation volume, blend uniformity, and %CDR). The designed SOS-CDS was evaluated for its stability and other physicochemical parameters. BATA model was utilized to assess the taste masking of carbamazepine. Results DSC and FTIR spectra showed no interaction between the drug and excipients. Optimized SOS-CDS showed good micromeritics properties and a desired sedimentation volume, with 93.7% release at 420 min. BATA model revealed the taste masking of CBZ. Conclusion The major concern with the current formulation was its instability in the presence of light and moisture. The developed SOS-CDS was stable due to its intelligent mechanism. In addition, long-term use of CBZ causes bone degeneration, which may be overcome by supplementing Vitamin D. Liquorice was explored as a masking agent for the bitter taste of CBZ and was confirmed in the BATA model. The newer SOS-CDS was stable and had controlled release. The developed formulation will be useful at an industrial scale.

The designed SOS-CDS was evaluated for its stability and other physicochemical parameters. Results DSC and FTIR spectra showed no interaction between the drug and excipients.

papers.title: Disentangled Ultrahigh-Molecular-Weight Polyethylene by Boroxide Complexes of Half-Titanocenes via Hydrogen Bonding Interaction
papers.abstract: Abstract The disentangled state of ultrahigh-molecular-weight polyethylene (UHMWPE) is of practical importance to its processability, but the direct synthesis of disentangled UHMWPE (dis-UHMWPE) remains highly challenging. Herein, a series of half-titanocenes Cp′Ti(L)Cl2 (Cp′ = cyclopentadienyl derivatives; L = (Ar2)BO–) bearing electron-withdrawing boroxide ancillary ligands have been developed for ethylene polymerization. Although the steric and electronic modifications of Cp′ and boroxide ancillary ligands impact catalytic activity, the substituted boroxide-containing half-titanocenes produce UHMWPE with viscosity-average molecular weights (Mv) of >1 × 106 g/mol under regular polymerization conditions. The resultant UHMWPEs feature a low degree of chain entanglement as confirmed by differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) annealing studies and melt rheological tests. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations further reveal that the formation of dis-UHMWPE originates from the hydrogen bonding interaction between the electron-withdrawing boroxide ancillary ligand and β-H on the growing polymer chain, which promotes chain growth and suppresses β-H elimination chain transfer.

papers.title: Rice starch–activated carbon composite films for potential cosmetic facial sheet mask applications: physicochemical and mechanical characterization
papers.abstract: Abstract The widespread use of synthetic facial sheet masks has raised concerns about their environmental impact. In this study, rice starch (RS)–activated carbon (AC) composite films were prepared by solution casting and characterized to assess their potential as biodegradable cosmetic mask substrates. The surface morphology of the films changed after AC incorporation, with thicknesses ranging from approximately 0.2 to 0.3 mm and the moisture content increasing with increasing AC loading. The water contact angles ranged from 48.95° to 63.85°, indicating hydrophilic surfaces, with the RS + AC (0.4 g) film exhibiting the lowest measured contact angle. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy suggested predominantly physical interactions between the RS and AC, whereas differential scanning calorimetry and X-ray diffraction characterized their thermal transitions and structural features. Compared with the neat RS film, the RS + AC (0.4 g) film exhibited lower tensile strength and elongation at break. MTT assays performed on AC powder revealed that the cell viability of L929 fibroblasts and HaCaT keratinocytes was above 90% under the tested conditions; the complete composite films were not evaluated for cytotoxicity. Soil burial testing revealed approximately 68.7% mass loss for the RS + AC film after 30 days. These findings support further investigations of RS + AC films as biodegradable cosmetic mask substrates. Their biocompatibility, water uptake, serum retention, and performance during skin application remain to be established.

papers.title: Equol–Thiophene‐Based Benzoxazine: Synthesis, Curing Kinetics, and Blend Properties
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT A novel biobased bifunctional benzoxazine monomer EQ‐tma was successfully synthesized via Mannich condensation using equol and 2‐thiophenemethylamine as starting materials. The chemical structure of the monomer was confirmed by 1 H NMR, 13 C NMR, FT‐IR, and high‐resolution mass spectrometry. The curing kinetics of EQ‐tma were investigated by non‐isothermal DSC, and the apparent activation energies determined by the Kissinger, Ozawa, and Starink methods were 93.94, 97.21, and 87.50 kJ/mol, respectively, indicating that the curing reaction followed an autocatalytic model, and the kinetic equation was accordingly established. EQ‐tma was then blended with commercial PH‐ddm, and the curing mechanism of the blends was studied by in situ FT‐IR. TGA analysis demonstrated that the incorporation of EQ‐tma improved the thermal stability of the commercial benzoxazine, while DMA was employed to evaluate the thermomechanical properties of the resultant co‐polymers. This study provides new insights into the molecular design of biobased benzoxazines and reveals their formulation potential when blended with benzoxazine commercial system.

papers.title: RECENT ADVANCES IN MUCOADHESIVE MICROSPHERES FOR ORAL CONTROLLED DRUG DELIVERY: FORMULATION STRATEGIES, CHARACTERIZATION, THERAPEUTIC APPLICATIONS AND FUTURE PERSPECTIVES
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Mucoadhesive microspheres have emerged as one of the most promising oral controlled drug delivery systems due to their ability to prolong gastrointestinal residence time, improve drug bioavailability, and enhance patient compliance. These multiparticulate systems adhere to the mucosal surface, thereby extending drug absorption and minimizing dosing frequency. Various natural and synthetic polymers, including Carbopol, Chitosan, Hydroxypropyl Methylcellulose (HPMC), Sodium Alginate, and Eudragit polymers, have been extensively investigated for the preparation of mucoadhesive microspheres. Different preparation techniques such as solvent evaporation, ionotropic gelation, spray drying, and emulsion cross-linking have been successfully employed to formulate microspheres with desirable physicochemical characteristics. The performance of these systems is evaluated through particle size analysis, drug entrapment efficiency, swelling behavior, mucoadhesive strength, zeta potential, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR), Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC), and in-vitro drug release studies. Mucoadhesive microspheres have been successfully used for antihypertensive, anti-diabetic, antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, and anticancer medications, according to recent studies. Research on mucoadhesive microspheres loaded with nifedipine has demonstrated longer therapeutic efficacy, better entrapment efficiency, and sustained drug release, suggesting their potential for controlled oral drug administration. There are still issues with large-scale production, reproducibility, regulatory approval, and long-term stability despite tremendous advancements. Future studies should concentrate on Quality by Design (QbD), artificial intelligence-based formulation optimization, smart polymers, and mucoadhesive systems aided by nanotechnology.

papers.title: Effects of nitrogen rates and pulsed versus continuous subsurface drip irrigation on gas exchange in sugarcane
papers.abstract: Abstract The pulse irrigation presents itself as a strategy capable of contributing to the efficient management of water and nitrogen, resulting in the optimization of agricultural cultivation. The objective of this study was to evaluate the influence of the application of nitrogen doses, applied via pulse and continuous fertigation, on gas exchange in sugarcane crops. For this, a field experiment was set up at the Carpina Sugarcane Experimental Station (EECAC) in the State of Pernambuco, Brazil. The experimental design was randomized blocks, in a 5 × 2 factorial scheme, with five nitrogen doses (80, 120, 160, 240 and 320 kg ha − 1 ) and two types of irrigation application (pulse and continuous), with four replicates. At 240 and 300 DAH, gas exchange evaluations were performed. Pulse irrigation combined with an estimated N dose of 189.4 kg ha − 1 , determined through regression analysis, promoted higher net photosynthesis in sugarcane. Applying nitrogen doses higher than 168.4 kg ha − 1 reduced carboxylation efficiency and water use, indicating a physiological limit for the nutrient. Pulse irrigation improved net photosynthesis, transpiration, stomatal conductance, internal CO 2 concentration, instantaneous water use efficiency, intrinsic water use efficiency and instantaneous carboxylation efficiency, highlighting the potential of integrated management of irrigation and nitrogen fertilization in the physiological performance of the crop.

papers.title: The future of salicylic acid in agriculture lies in precision priming
papers.abstract: As the world is moving towards enforcing strict regulations against pesticides, plant hormones triggering natural defenses represent a foundation of sustainable agriculture. Among them, Salicylic acid (SA) is a major phytohormone for governing systemic acquired resistance (SAR), a broad-spectrum immune response, against hemibiotrophic and biotrophic pathogens. Although it has huge potential as a sustainable alternative to synthetic pesticides, its field efficacy lags, with inconsistent disease control, phytotoxicity, and significant yield loss. This review gathers emerging evidence to explain the inconsistency of SA-mediated disease control under field conditions and proposes priming-based frameworks to improve reliability in crop protection systems. It focuses on two underexplored areas. First, the metabolic and hormonal basis of the growth-defense trade-off. Second, the climate-induced signaling failure, where elevated temperatures disrupt the SA transcriptional machinery. Simultaneously, the review explores emerging innovative strategies, such as nano-formulations for controlled release, synthetic analogues with enhanced stability, and the paradigm shift from direct induction to molecular priming to solve the existing problems. By integrating findings from the model and crop species, we infer that the future of SA in agriculture does not lie in direct, high-dose application in the field. Instead, it lies in the development of intelligent, climate-resilient priming systems that work in alignment with plant biology.

papers.title: Integrated microbiome and metabolomic analysis reveals associations between vaginal microbiota composition and psychological profiles
papers.abstract: The vaginal microbiota plays a key role in women’s health and is increasingly linked to psychobiological processes, although underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study investigated the relationship between vaginal community state types (CSTs), psychological dimensions, and vaginal metabolites in 105 reproductive-aged women. Vaginal microbiota composition was characterised through 16 S rRNA gene sequencing and classified into CSTs; metabolomic profiling was performed using NMR spectroscopy. Participants completed validated questionnaires assessing trait anxiety, emotion regulation, behavioural inhibition/activation, depressive symptoms, perceived stress, and somatisation. Women with polymicrobial CST IV profiles showed significantly lower Behavioural Activation System (BAS)-Reward Responsiveness and BAS-Drive scores, whereas those with Lactobacillus iners -dominated CST III exhibited lower Behavioural Inhibition System (BIS) scores. Limited direct correlations between bacterial taxa and psychological variables emerged, but psychological dimensions strongly correlated with specific vaginal metabolites. Exploratory mediation analyses indicated that aminobutyrate and valine partially or fully mediated the associations between CST IV and BAS dimensions, while phenylalanine partially mediated the relationship between CST IV and BIS inhibition. These findings suggest that the vaginal metabolome may represent a functional interface linking microbial community structure and psychological functioning, supporting a biopsychosocial perspective of vaginal health and the importance of integrating microbiome, metabolomic, and psychological assessments in women’s health research.

papers.title: Atom‐Efficient Cerium‐Based Molecular Cages as Biocompatible Reactive Oxygen Scavengers
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The development of reactive oxygen species (ROS)‐scavenging materials for biomedical applications has been constrained by the difficulty associated with achieving simultaneously broad‐spectrum scavenging efficiency and acceptable biosafety. To date, ceria/nanoceria systems have been explored for this purpose; however, they suffer from limited cerium‐atom utilization. Inspired by the atom‐economy concept of single‐atom catalysis, we report a cerium‐based molecular‐cage strategy for treating oxidative stress‐driven atherosclerosis (AS). It involves mixed‐valent cerium ions (Ce 3+ /Ce 4+ ) that are stably confined within tailored molecular cages and that mimic the cooperation between oxygen vacancies and cerium redox cycling in CeO 2 . This endows the four representative cages of this study with an ability to scavenge superoxide anion (O 2 • − ), hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ), and hydroxyl radical (•OH). Their catalytic function can be readily modulated through the ROS‐responsive release of the molecular cages at local lesion sites. This capability was found to alleviate oxidative stress and associated inflammation, as inferred from the finding that a lead cerium cage incorporated into a biocompatible nanoparticle reduces the progression of AS in a mouse model. A reduction in plaque lipid deposition, macrophage accumulation, necrotic core formation, and MMP‐9‐associated matrix was seen.

papers.title: PLA/BioAlSr composite films for tendon–bone interface regeneration: effect of bioactive glass content on morphology, mechanical behavior, degradation and bioactivity
papers.journal: Journal of Applied Materials and Technology
papers.abstract: One of the major challenges in implant materials engineering is combining mechanical strength, moldability, biocompatibility, bioresorbability, and osteoactivity within a single material. This work develops poly(lactic acid) (PLA) films loaded with a strontium- and alumina-containing bioactive glass (BioAlSr), explored as a candidate material for metallic-implant coatings and, prospectively, tendon–bone interface grafts. Melt-quenched glass powder (mean diameter 5 µm) was incorporated at 15, 30, 50 and 70 wt% by solvent casting. Characterization covered microscopy with TGA, EDS, XRD, tensile testing, swelling in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) with pH monitoring, cytotoxicity and bioactivity in simulated body fluid (SBF). Particles were mechanically embedded, with no evidence of strong interfacial bonding. Tensile strength peaked at 15 wt% (15 ± 1 MPa) and fell sharply already by 30 wt% (6.1 ± 1.3 MPa), continuing to decline at 50–70 wt% (3 ± 2 to 2.5 ± 6 MPa); elongation at break fell from 61 ± 17 % for neat PLA to 13 % at 15–30 wt% and below 5 % at 50–70 wt%, while Young's modulus (63–72 MPa) was comparatively insensitive to glass content. After 28 days in PBS, swelling ranged from 2.1 % (30 wt%) to 8.6 % (70 wt%) against 2.7 % for neat PLA, and pH rose from 7.2 to 9.0–10.6 for loadings ? 30 wt%, remaining near 7.3 for neat PLA and 15 wt%. In neutral red uptake, undiluted extract gave 89 % viability for 15 wt% and 66 % for 30 wt%, against 46 % for neat PLA (NCTC clone 929); the 50 and 70 wt% films reduced viability to 63 % at 100 mg mL?¹ (NIH/3T3). No composite reached IC50, and all were less cytotoxic than neat PLA. After SBF immersion, all glass-loaded films developed a crystalline calcium-phosphate phase while EDS confirmed progressive Ca and P surface enrichment, supporting apatite-like mineralization. Glass content therefore trades mechanical performance against degradation and bioactivity; 15–30 wt% was retained as the working range for its favorable combination of tensile strength and particle-dispersion homogeneity relative to 50–70 wt%, notwithstanding PVBio30's cytotoxicity falling marginally below the ISO 10993-5 threshold.

papers.title: Seed balls with bauxite mining technosol: an alternative forest restoration technique in the Brazilian Atlantic Forest
papers.abstract: Abstract This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of technosol, composed of clay cake and organic compost, as a substrate for seed balls using native species from the Atlantic Forest. We investigated how different substrate compositions and the addition of NPK fertilizer influence the emergence, survival, and growth of four native tree species: Senna macranthera , Enterolobium contortisiliquum , Pterogyne nitens , and Anadenanthera peregrina . Seedling emergence and survival were monitored continuously over 190 days, and growth performance was evaluated using logistic growth models. The results showed that, in terms of emergence and survival, treatments without NPK addition yielded the best outcomes, regardless of the proportion of clay cake and organic compost. Growth models revealed that non-pioneer species ( P. nitens and A. peregrina ) performed better under treatments without NPK, while pioneer species ( S. macranthera and E. contortisiliquum ) exhibited higher growth rates in treatments with NPK. These findings emphasize the importance of aligning substrate composition and fertilization with the ecological strategies of different species to optimize restoration outcomes. The use of technosol-based seed balls derived from bauxite mining represents a viable alternative for forest restoration, promoting biodiversity recovery, reducing waste disposal in tailings dams, and contributing to circular economy principles in the mining sector.

papers.title: Eyegent: Visual Attention Orchestration on Concepts
papers.abstract: Abstract Where a human looks is not random, nor is it merely a reflex to visual salience. It is a decision shaped by goals, constrained by language, and driven by the need to resolve uncertainty. We propose Eyegent , an active vision agent built on this premise: that visual search is best understood as sequential Bayesian inference over semantically grounded hypotheses, with fixations serving as epistemic actions. Given an image and a natural-language query, Eyegent constructs a discrete hypothesis space of candidate segmentation masks, maintains an explicit posterior belief distribution, and selects each fixation to maximise expected information gain—updating beliefs via vision–language model verification and terminating when uncertainty falls below a principled risk threshold. We formalise this process as Bayesian Active Semantic Grounding (BASG), a computational-level account that provides formal guarantees on belief concentration, entropy reduction, and bounded decision risk. The framework is neurobiologically grounded in the large-scale network organisation of the human brain, with the Salience Network identified as the dynamic orchestrator of semantic, inferential, and oculomotor processes. Critically, Eyegent requires no gaze supervision and no task-specific training: it is zero-shot, modular, and built entirely from off-the-shelf components. Evaluated on RefCOCO-Gaze and AiR-D, two benchmarks coupling language-driven visual tasks with human eye-tracking ground truth, Eyegent achieves competitive or state-of-the-art performance among zero-shot methods across semantic, spatial, and structural scanpath metrics, and approaches supervised baselines on several dimensions. The result is a system that does not merely predict where humans look, but generates scanpaths for the same reason humans generate them: to find out.

papers.title: PHARMACOSOMAL GEL FORMULATION OF ACECLOFENAC : DESIGN, OPTIMIZATION AND EVALUATION
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Aceclofenac is a widely used non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug; however, its poor aqueous solubility may limit effective drug delivery. The present study aimed to develop and optimize Aceclofenac-loaded Pharmacosomes using a Quality by Design (QbD) approach and incorporate the optimized formulation into a topical gel. Pharmacosomes were prepared by the solvent evaporation method using soya lecithin and chloroform. A Central Composite Design (CCD) was employed to investigate the effects of formulation variables. Preformulation studies, including melting point, UV spectroscopy, FTIR and DSC, were performed. The prepared Pharmacosomes were evaluated for particle size, zeta potential, entrapment efficiency, drug content and in-vitro drug release. Release kinetics and numerical optimization were carried out using Design-Expert® software. The optimized formulation was incorporated into Carbopol 934 gel and evaluated for pH, viscosity, spreadability, extrudability and drug content. Aceclofenac exhibited a melting point of 150°C and a DSC endothermic peak at 147.65°C. The calibration curve demonstrated good linearity (R² = 0.9996), while FTIR studies indicated drug–excipient compatibility. The optimized Pharmacosomes exhibited a particle size of 187.52 nm and a zeta potential of −24.9 mV. Entrapment efficiency and drug content ranged from 78.46–91.49% and 83.58–94.55%, respectively. Controlled drug release was observed for up to 8 hours. Numerical optimization identified 434 mg soya lecithin, 15 mL chloroform and 90 minutes hydration time, with a desirability of 0.880. The optimized gel exhibited a pH of 6.73, viscosity of 5463 ± 3.42 cps, spreadability of 13.47 ± 0.53 g·cm/sec and drug content of 93.48 ± 0.06%. Intermediate stability studies indicated satisfactory stability of the optimized formulation.

papers.title: Investigation of static and dynamic mechanical properties of graphene-based thermoplastic polyurethane nanocomposites: Experimental and MD simulation approach
papers.abstract: Recent advancements in multiscale analysis are essential for developing high-quality polymer nanocomposites (PNCs) with tailored thermo-mechanical and viscoelastic behaviour. In the current work, a dual approach combining experimental methods and non-equilibrium molecular dynamics (NEMD) simulations enable a thorough evaluation of the material’s performance. This approach provides deeper insights into the influence of graphene (Gr) at the atomic scale and validates these effects at the macroscale. Here, experimental tensile and dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA) testing, paired with NEMD simulations, are used to explore both the static and dynamic mechanical behaviours of Gr-based thermoplastic polyurethane (Gr/TPU) nanocomposites. Tensile and DMA testing results indicate that adding 3 wt % of graphene (Gr) to TPU increases the yield strength by 53.06% and the storage modulus by 17.20%, respectively. Notably, the glass transition temperature (T g ) shifts towards a higher value in the 3 wt% Gr/TPU nanocomposite. Due to weak interfacial interactions and high chain mobility, increasing the Gr content at higher temperatures triggers a decrease in the storage modulus while increasing both the loss tangent and loss modulus. This improvement in the damping factor (tan δ) makes these PNCs promising candidates for applications requiring shock absorption in engineering components.
papers.summary: Recent advancements in multiscale analysis are essential for developing high-quality polymer nanocomposites (PNCs) with tailored thermo-mechanical and viscoelastic behaviour. Tensile and DMA testing results indicate that adding 3 wt % of graphene (Gr) to TPU increases the yield strength by 53.06% and the storage modulus by 17.20%, respectively.

papers.abstract: Fiber of oil palm trunk from selected tree trunks of a plantation in Nigeria was treated with 5% NaOH aqueous solution to improve its surface characteristics, dried, sorted and used to reinforce polypropylene matrix used to form a composite for insulating thermal flask. Loadings of palm trunk fibre were varied as 10%, 20%, 30% and 40% in polypropylene matrix. Raw and treated oil palm trunk fibre samples were subjected to chemical, mechanical and physical analyses to determine composition, density, hardness, impact and tensile strengths in accordance with ASTM D638 standard using standard equipment. Composite samples were subjected to tests such as hardness, density, impact, tensile strength, thermo-gravimetric and thermal conductivity with equipment that included injection moulding machine, Instron tensile tester, Tinius impact machine, Rockwell hardness tester, Perkin Elmer instrument and Lees disc apparatus accessed at different institutional laboratories. papers.title: Programmed Drug Release from Triple Stimuli-Responsive Poly( N -vinylcaprolactam)- b -Poly(ε-caprolactone) Copolymer Nanoassemblies with Enhanced Encapsulation through Noncovalent Interactions in the Core
papers.abstract: Abstract Multi-stimuli-responsive biodegradable polymeric nanoassemblies with high encapsulation ability, micellar stability, and programmed intracellular drug release are highly attractive for efficient cancer therapy. Herein, an amphiphilic diblock copolymer responsive to three endogenous stimuli of a cancer cell is synthesized using temperature-responsive poly(N-vinylcaprolactam) as a macroinitiator for the ring-opening polymerization of chloroalkyl-substituted ε-caprolactone. Phenyl and triazole rings are incorporated in the side chain to link a redox-responsive disulfide group to a hydrophobic block using click chemistry. The diblock copolymer self-assembles in aqueous medium into spherical micelles with an average hydrodynamic diameter of 140–150 nm. High dye encapsulation efficiency and stability are verified by fluorescence resonance energy transfer and isothermal titration calorimetry studies. Copolymer nanoassemblies display ill-defined aggregates at tumor-relevant temperatures (40–43 °C), glutathione-induced swelling, and esterase-mediated complete micellar disassembly. Combined effect of triple stimuli on drug release is observed compared to the release in response to individual stimuli. The diblock copolymer shows excellent biocompatibility with MCF-7 and MDA-MB-231 cancer cells, and DOX-loaded copolymer nanoassemblies show cytotoxicity toward the cancer cells, augmented by low IC50 values (6.37 and 4.58 μg/mL). Cellular uptake and time-dependent drug release in cancer cells are demonstrated.

papers.title: Matrigel scaffold, alone or with human placenta-derived mesenchymal stromal cells, improves histological repair of murine excisional wounds
papers.abstract: Impaired cutaneous wound healing remains a major clinical challenge, particularly when excessive inflammation disrupts tissue regeneration and extracellular matrix remodeling. Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs; the term recommended by the International Society for Cell & Gene Therapy in preference to “mesenchymal stem cells”) have been proposed as therapeutic agents on the basis of their immunomodulatory and paracrine properties. Human placenta-derived mesenchymal stromal cells (hPMSCs) are of particular interest because of their accessibility, proliferative capacity and low reported immunogenicity. Whether their benefit in cutaneous wounds is attributable to the cells themselves, to the delivery vehicle, or to both, has not been resolved. In this preclinical study, two full-thickness excisional wounds were created on the dorsum of female BALB/c mice and treated by intradermal injection with hPMSCs alone, hPMSCs incorporated within a Matrigel scaffold, Matrigel alone, or vehicle (DMEM) control. Separate cohorts were euthanized on days 7, 14 and 21 post-wounding ( n = 5 mice, 10 wounds, per group per time point). Wound repair was assessed by histological and histomorphometric analysis of haematoxylin and eosin and Masson’s trichrome-stained sections. Collagen density was quantified morphometrically from Masson’s trichrome-stained sections, and re-epithelialization was graded on a five-point ordinal scale. Inflammatory cell infiltration and skin appendage regeneration were described qualitatively and were not quantified; inflammatory cells were not counted, and serial macroscopic wound-area measurements were not performed. Serum interleukin-10 (IL-10), interleukin-17 (IL-17) and interferon-γ (IFN-γ) were measured by ELISA on days 7, 14 and 21 as indices of the systemic inflammatory response. All three treatments improved histological repair relative to vehicle control. At day 21, collagen density was 86.1 ± 7.5% in the hPMSC + Matrigel group, compared with 77.8 ± 6.6% for Matrigel alone, 68.4 ± 5.1% for hPMSCs alone and 45.1 ± 4.1% for vehicle control. Across the three time points, the improvement in collagen density observed with Matrigel alone was 80–93% as large as the combination-versus-vehicle difference when the group means were compared descriptively. Adding hPMSCs to the scaffold gave a modest further increase of 5.8, 3.8 and 8.3% points at days 7, 14 and 21, which remained significant after Bonferroni adjustment only at day 7. The combination showed the highest re-epithelialization grade and the most organized dermal architecture on qualitative histological assessment at day 21. Systemically, hPMSC administration was associated with elevated serum IL-10 and reduced IFN-γ relative to control, with little difference in IL-17. In this model, a Matrigel scaffold improved histological wound repair relative to vehicle; adding hPMSCs to the scaffold gave a modest further increase in collagen density, and the combination performed best of the conditions tested. Because the study includes no non-MSC cellular control, the incremental benefit of the cells over the scaffold cannot be attributed specifically to hPMSC identity; and because no local (wound-bed) immunological or angiogenic analysis was performed, the accompanying serum cytokine changes represent a systemic association rather than a demonstrated local immunomodulatory mechanism. These findings should be regarded as an initial preclinical observation supporting combined cell–scaffold delivery, which requires confirmation with an appropriate cellular control and direct assessment of the wound microenvironment.

papers.title: Production and Characterization of Biodegradable Packaging Composites from Recycled Expanded Polystyrene Filled with Groundnut Shell Cassava Peel Powders
papers.journal: Journal of Science Research and Reviews
papers.abstract: This study reports the production and characterization of biodegradable packaging materials made from recycled expanded polystyrene (REPS) filled with alkali-treated groundnut shell powder (GNSP) and cassava peel powder (CPP) as a green alternative to conventional Styrofoam, which are usually disposed in landfills or burnt in incinerator, resulting in material loss, emission of toxic and carcinogenic substances into the atmosphere, harming the environment and human life. Composite samples (A-E) were formulated with a fixed REPS, GNSP and varying CPP content, compounded on a two-roll mill and formed by compression moulding. The composites were characterized using thermogravimetric analysis, scanning electron microscopy, and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, and evaluated for tensile, impact, hardness, flexural, density, water absorption, and soil-burial biodegradability properties. TGA showed a multi-stage thermal decomposition profile for all composite specimens compared with the single-stage profile of the control, denoting reduced thermal stability with increasing filler content. SEM revealed homogeneous filler distribution at intermediate loading (Sample B) and agglomeration with crack formation at higher loading (Sample E). FTIR confirmed hydroxyl and carbonyl groups associated with the natural fillers. Tensile properties improved initially in Sample A (27.66 MPa), with Sample B recording the highest tensile strength (29.22 MPa), while Sample C gave the highest impact strength (0.183 J/mm) and flexural modulus (2686.93 MPa), after which performance declined at higher loadings. Density and hardness decreased, while water absorption increased, with increasing filler content. Biodegradation tests after 63 days showed progressive weight loss from the control to Sample E, with Sample C recording the highest weight loss (0.705%), confirming that natural fillers render the composites more susceptible to microbial attack and thereby enhance biodegradability.

papers.title: Exploring the thermal and mechanical performance of hybrid bio composites reinforced with agro waste fibers and Turbinella pyrum shell powder
papers.abstract: Abstract The use of sustainable natural fiber-reinforced polymer composites has attracted considerable attention mainly because they are environmentally friendly and can replace heavy components in engineering. The present work involves making hybrid epoxy composites reinforced with banana stem fiber (BSF), sugarcane bagasse fiber (SCF), and Turbinella pyrum shell (TPS) powder by the vacuum-assisted resin infusion technique. Nine composite samples (S1-S9) were made by changing fiber and TPS filler amounts to study the mechanical, thermal, moisture resistance, and morphological properties of the composites. The study found that the addition of the TPS filler might be the biggest reason for the composite’s better performance, which increased with filler content up to a maximum of 3 wt%. S6 showed the best tensile strength (20.0 MPa), tensile modulus (2.95 GPa), flexural strength (49.8 MPa), flexural modulus (4.48 GPa), and impact strength (8.1 kJ/m 2 ); these properties were 332.9%, 136.0%, 255.7%, 250.0%, and approximately 523.1% better than the unfilled S1 formulation. S5, in contrast, has the highest compressive strength (9.40 MPa), compressive modulus (1.34 GPa), and minimum moisture absorption (1.95%), which indicates very good resistance to water. The composite formulation with the lowest weight and highest strength was selected, based on different performance criteria (mechanical, thermal, and moisture resistance), by multi-response optimization. It was revealed that S6 was the composite formulation showing the most balanced characteristics. Thermogravimetric studies showed that the composites with TPS filler have better thermal capability, and SEM imaging revealed discrepancies among composite samples for fibre pull-out, void presence, filler dispersion, and the nature of the crack. EDX analysis was used to detect the calcium carbonate (CaCO 3 ) enriched material of the TPS filler, and its contribution towards the increase of composites’ stiffness and thermal resistance was acknowledged. These results portray the possibility of using TPS-filled hybrid epoxy composites as green products for lightweight structural and engineering applications.

papers.title: When active learning fails, uncalibrated out of distribution uncertainty quantification might be the problem
papers.abstract: Abstract Efficiently and meaningfully estimating prediction uncertainty is important for exploration in active learning campaigns in materials discovery, where samples with high uncertainty are interpreted as containing information missing from the model. In this work, the effect of different uncertainty estimation and calibration methods are evaluated for active learning when using ensembles of ALIGNN, eXtreme Gradient Boost, Random Forest, and Neural Network model architectures. We compare uncertainty estimates from ALIGNN deep ensembles to loss landscape uncertainty estimates obtained for solubility, bandgap, and formation energy prediction tasks. We then evaluate how the quality of the uncertainty estimate impacts an active learning campaign that seeks model generalization to out-of-distribution data. Uncertainty calibration methods were found to variably generalize from in-domain data to out-of-domain data. Furthermore, calibrated uncertainties were generally unsuccessful in reducing the amount of data required by a model to improve during an active learning campaign on out-of-distribution data when compared to random sampling and uncalibrated uncertainties. The impact of poor-quality uncertainty persists for random forest and eXtreme Gradient Boosting models trained on the same data for the same tasks, indicating that this is at least partially intrinsic to the data and not due to model capacity alone. Analysis of the target, in-distribution uncertainty, out-of-distribution uncertainty, and training residual distributions suggest that future work focus on understanding empirical uncertainties in the feature input space for cases where ensemble prediction variances do not accurately capture the missing information required for the model to generalize.

papers.title: ПЕРЕДОВАЯ ДИАГНОСТИКА И ТЕРАПИЯ МЕТАБОЛИЧЕСКОЙ ДИСФУНКЦИИ У БОЛЬНЫХ С СЕПСИСОМ
papers.abstract: Цель исследования — применение современных методов диагностики и терапии метаболической дисфункции у больных с сепсисом для рационализации лечения и улучшения его исходов. Материалы и методы. Обследованы 11 больных с сепсисом, получавших в послеоперационном периоде лечебное питание смесью «Нутризет Д», содержащей многокомпонентный метабиотический комплекс и β-глюканы. Оценка метаболизма осуществлялась с помощью специализированной диагностической системы. Результаты. У пациентов регистрировалось уменьшение проявлений полиорганного синдрома, воспаления, питательной недостаточности, энергопотребности и дисбиоза, а также улучшение гуморального иммунитета и дыхательного коэффициента (RQ), указывающего на метаболизм основных макронутриентов, во все сроки исследования. Корреляционный анализ обнаружил ассоциации шкалы SOFA с прокальцитонином. Фиксированы связи прокальцитонина и С-реактивного белка, а также альбумина с трансферрином. Идентифицированы ассоциации IgG с лактобактериями, IgM с бифидобактериями, альбумина с лактобактериями и IgA с бифидобактериями. Заключение. У больных с сепсисом, находящихся на искусственной вентиляции легких, оправдано осуществление метода непрямой калориметрии для мониторинга расхода калорий и RQ, определяющих адресность назначенного лечебного питания как с позиций его качественного и количественного состава, так и с позиций объема и скорости вводимой питательной смеси. Мониторинг расхода калорий и RQ позволяет оценить метаболизм макронутриентов, поступающих в организм больного при реализации конкретного лечебного питания, которые используются им для получения энергии. Анализ вариабельности расхода калорий и типа метаболизма вводимых питательных субстратов необходим для аттестации продуктивности их утилизации и подтверждения правильности выбора используемой питательной смеси. Мониторинг затрат энергии и RQ служит ключевой информацией для адресной рационализации лечебного питания. У пациентов с сепсисом целесообразно использование лечебного питания, содержащего в своем составе многокомпонентный метабиотический комплекс и β-глюканы, для устранения дефицита нутриентов и микробиоты кишечника, метаболической и системных дисфункций, а также модуляции иммунного ответа.

papers.title: The Community Capitals Dataset: Quantifying the Community Capitals Framework in the United States
papers.abstract: The Community Capitals Framework offers a systematic approach to community development, conceptualizing vibrant communities as the product of a cohesive system derived from built, cultural, financial, human, natural, political, and social capitals. For more than twenty years, the Framework has been successfully applied in both research and practice, but a persistent challenge for both is navigating how to quantify each of the seven capitals. In this article, we propose a novel dataset at the U.S. county-level to address this challenge. We synthesize the literature that has shaped the Community Capitals Framework and narrate a path forward in quantifying each at the county-level using publicly available data. We make this Community Capitals Dataset publicly available to facilitate further use and development of the Community Capitals Framework.

papers.title: Solution Behavior of Semiflexible Polyelectrolyte Carboxymethylcellulose with Anisotropic Counterions That Have Spatially Separated Charges
papers.abstract: Abstract The properties of polyelectrolytes depend on the counterions that neutralize their backbone. Although the effects of counterion valence and size have been studied, the influence of charge topology, i.e., the spatial distribution of charge within a multivalent counterion, has not been investigated experimentally. We address this question by comparing aqueous solutions of carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) containing conventional divalent metal ions with solutions containing the organic ditopic counterions hexamethonium and suxamethonium. Conductivity measurements indicate comparable counterion dissociation at low polymer concentrations but substantially greater dissociation of the ditopic ions at higher concentrations. SAXS measurements reveal corresponding structural differences: CMC with ditopic counterions exhibits correlation peaks and smaller stretching parameters, consistent with a larger effective polymer charge and reduced local chain folding, whereas CMC with monotopic divalent metal counterions displays broad correlation shoulders, consistent with weaker electrostatic correlations. Partially “dangling” condensed ditopic ions provide a possible explanation for the observation that the monotopic and ditopic counterions show similar fractions of free counterions from conductivity at low concentrations, while the SAXS profiles indicate a higher effective charge for the ditopic salts. However, this mechanism cannot be established unambiguously from the present conductivity and scattering measurements. Overall, the results demonstrate that counterion charge topology provides a tuneable parameter for controlling polyelectrolyte conformation and charge transport.

papers.title: A multivariate plasma biomarker model for glioblastoma exclusion: a retrospective case-control study
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Glioblastoma (GBM) remains the most aggressive primary brain tumour, with limited diagnostic tools able to capture its molecular heterogeneity in real time. Current clinical practice relies on MRI and invasive biopsies, which are poorly suited for early or dynamic disease monitoring. Sensitive and accessible blood-based biomarkers could offer a minimally invasive alternative to aid GBM diagnosis and exclusion. METHODS: In this retrospective case-control study, plasma concentrations of seven neurological and inflammatory proteins (GFAP, UCH-L1, NfL, Tau, NSE, MPO, and PMN elastase) were quantified in 72 GBM patients and 102 healthy individuals (NAB-X biobank, n = 20; Clinique Saint-Luc Bouge, n = 82, age-matched) using ultrasensitive immunoassay platforms, complemented by conventional clinical laboratory assays and standard ELISA methods. Diagnostic accuracy was evaluated through ROC analysis and logistic regression modelling, with internal validation performed by 10-fold cross-validation and bootstrap resampling. RESULTS: GFAP and NfL showed the highest individual discriminative performances (AUC = 0.995 and 0.957, respectively). A multivariate model integrating GFAP, NfL, Tau, NSE, MPO, and PMN elastase showed excellent discrimination between GBM and healthy controls (AUC = 0.999; sensitivity = 98.6%; specificity = 100%). The model's negative predictive value remained above 0.999 in simulated population settings, supporting its use as a potential high-sensitivity exclusion tool. CONCLUSIONS: This study reports the possibility of using a plasma-based multivariate biomarker framework to discriminate GBM from healthy individuals with high sensitivity, providing proof-of-concept evidence supporting the future development of a plasma-based exclusion tool. This needs validation in clinically representative symptomatic populations. By integrating astrocytic, neuronal, and inflammatory markers into a single logistic model, this approach bridges analytical precision with clinical applicability, paving the way for a minimally invasive blood test to support diagnostic rule-out in neuro-oncology.

papers.title: Mapping E-Readiness Dimensions for Digital Village Development: A Systematic Literature and Bibliometric Review
papers.journal: Journal of Information Systems and Informatics
papers.abstract: Digital village development is a key strategy for narrowing the digital gap between rural and urban areas, yet research on e-readiness in this context remains fragmented and predominantly shaped by technical perspectives. This study maps e-readiness dimensions, identifies research trends, and uncovers research gaps in digital villages scholarship. A Systematic Literature Review (SLR) following the PRISMA 2020 framework was conducted on 55 articles published between 2020 and 2026, combining thematic synthesis with an author-keyword co-occurrence bibliometric analysis using VOSviewer. Five principal dimensions of e-readiness were identified: infrastructure and technology, human resources and digital literacy, social and cultural factors, governance and policy, and psychological and individual dimensions. The infrastructure and technology dimension remains the most dominant, reflecting a persistent technical bias not yet matched by attention to social, governance, and psychological readiness factors. Bibliometric analysis shows the research theme continues to be dominated by keywords such as digital transformation, digitalization, digital readiness, and smart village, while social aspects, governance, citizen participation, psychological factors, and rural development outcomes remain relatively underexplored. This research offers a multidimensional mapping of e-readiness for digital village development, framed using a socio-technical readiness perspective as a conceptual synthesis that requires further empirical validation.

papers.title: Impact of water-to-binder ratio on the physical, mechanical and durability-related performance of industrial waste-based one-part geopolymer concrete
papers.abstract: The development of just-add-water geopolymer technology offers a sustainable alternative to conventional alkali-activated systems by eliminating the handling risks associated with corrosive alkaline solutions. This study investigates the effect of the water-to-binder (W/B) ratio on the fresh, mechanical, durability, and microstructural properties of a one-part geopolymer concrete (OPGC) produced using a binary blend of industrial by-products, namely Magnesium Slag (MS) and Ground Granulated Blast Furnace Slag (GGBS). Five mixtures with W/B ratios ranging from 0.42 to 0.60 were prepared using a binder composition of 30% MS and 70% GGBS activated by solid sodium metasilicate. The results show that increasing the W/B ratio significantly improves workability but leads to reductions in density and compressive strength beyond an optimum W/B ratio of 0.47, which achieved the highest 28-day compressive strength of 54 MPa. Durability results indicated that water absorption decreased as the W/B ratio approached the optimum level of 0.47, which promoted better matrix continuity and reduced pore connectivity. However, further increases in the W/B ratio led to higher capillary porosity and increased water absorption. High-temperature exposure at 600 °C and 900 °C revealed that mixtures with lower W/B ratios experienced greater relative strength degradation, while higher W/B mixtures retained comparatively higher residual strength. SEM observations confirmed the transition from a compact gel matrix at low W/B ratios to a more porous and heterogeneous structure at higher W/B ratios.

papers.title: Study on gas flow characteristics and pulse blockage removal regulation in unstable collapsed boreholes
papers.abstract: Gas drainage boreholes easily suffer hole wall collapse and coal particle blockage under in-situ stress and mining disturbance, drastically lowering gas extraction efficiency. To avoid the drawbacks of traditional dredging technologies, including drainage interruption and borehole wall damage, a gas pulse blockage removal method is proposed to achieve non-contact dredging using transient high-pressure gas. By establishing a gas pulse dredging test system for collapsed and blocked boreholes, the flow resistance characteristics under the coupling effect of collapse position and coal particle size are revealed. The regulation mechanisms of pulse pressure and frequency on blockage removal performance are clarified, and prediction models for pore response and structural penetration degree are developed, considering energy attenuation and coal structure evolution. The results indicate that collapse position and particle size jointly determine borehole flow resistance. Fine coal blockage at the borehole opening creates a global flow bottleneck, bringing the lowest extraction peak concentration and serious gas retention in surrounding coal seams. Pulse energy decays exponentially with transmission distance: bottom-blocked boreholes show weak unblocking effect with response lag over 10 s, while orifice blockage responds rapidly and achieves prominent concentration growth. Pulse pressure presents a marginal diminishing promotion effect on dredging efficiency. Under the conditions of this experiment, 0.4 MPa is the optimal pressure for most conditions, with gas concentration increment ΔC reaching 110–186%; further increasing pressure to 0.6 MPa limits ΔC growth below 20.3%, and fine coal at the opening undergoes turbulent secondary deposition to weaken dredging effect. Pulse frequency dominates cumulative energy input, and unblocking performance evolves following a three-stage rule of slow growth, accelerated breakthrough and decelerated growth. The optimal frequency is 4 cycles per 10 min for middle-borehole collapse (ΔC increment of 94.7%) and 3 cycles per 10 min for orifice collapse (ΔC increment up to 168.0%). The model developed quantifies key parameters, showing that the comprehensive reaction coefficient A decreases as particle size increases, whilst the energy accumulation index B rises with increasing propagation distance. Based on this, a differentiated pulse strategy of ‘high-frequency, short-duration pulses near the source and low-frequency, cumulative pulses far from the source’ is proposed, which provides a theoretical basis and guidance on parameter design for the efficient and precise unblocking of gas extraction boreholes.

papers.title: Nonlinear characteristic analysis and MPC-based position control of a valve-controlled electro-hydraulic cylinder
papers.journal: Journal of Engineering and Applied Science
papers.abstract: Abstract This paper investigates how nonlinear hydraulic elasticity and LuGre-type friction affect the position tracking of a valve-controlled electro-hydraulic cylinder. An integrated electro-hydraulic position-servo model is established, including the power amplifier, servo valve, hydraulic actuator, displacement sensor, and feedback loop. Valve dead zone and hysteresis are treated as input-side nonlinearities, whereas the analysis focuses on cylinder-side oil compressibility and friction. The effects of bulk modulus, the nominal air-content parameter, Coulomb friction, viscous damping, and bristle stiffness are examined through MATLAB/Simulink-AMESIM co-simulation. A discrete MPC controller is then implemented in the MATLAB/Simulink MPC Toolbox using a transfer-function prediction model derived from the reduced-order electro-hydraulic position model. The internal prediction model is linear; hydraulic elasticity and LuGre friction remain in the nonlinear plant model and are not implemented as separate real-time feedforward compensation channels. The controller uses a sampling time of 0.02 s, a prediction horizon of 20 steps, a control horizon of 5 steps, and an output-related tuning weight of 0.06. Hardware experiments show that, compared with the tested proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controller, MPC reduces step-response overshoot from 0.22 mm to 0.04 mm for a 10 mm command and from 0.25 mm to 0.04 mm for a 20 mm command; the corresponding steady-state errors decrease from 0.35 mm to 0.20 mm and from 0.25 mm to 0.10 mm. For sinusoidal tracking at 3.14 rad/s and 6.28 rad/s, MPC reduces amplitude attenuation from 0.30 mm to 0.10 mm and from 0.55 mm to 0.15 mm, and phase lag from 18.0 degrees to 6.5 degrees and from 22.3 degrees to 10.1 degrees, respectively. The results demonstrate improved transient positioning and periodic tracking relative to PID under the investigated nonlinear plant conditions.

papers.title: Construction of a leak detection and pressure regulation system for municipal water distribution networks integrating digital twin technology
papers.abstract: Abstract Aging municipal water networks lose a substantial share of treated water to leakage, yet detection and pressure control are still pursued on separate models, so neither can inform the other. This paper builds an integrated system in which both functions read from and write to one continuously synchronized digital twin. The twin couples an open-source hydraulic kernel, a pressure-dependent demand closure and emitter-based leakage to an ensemble Kalman filter and a weighted least-squares recalibration step, so that heads, flows, Hazen–Williams roughness coefficients and demand multipliers are updated from multi-source telemetry rather than frozen at commissioning. Detection normalizes twin residuals against diurnal demand patterns and combines a sliding-window CUSUM statistic with a Mahalanobis joint test; the residual field then feeds a graph attention network that scores each junction and aggregates node posteriors into ranked suspect pipe segments. Regulation solves a bi-objective program over valve settings and pump speeds, weighting nodes by their leak posterior so that head is reduced hardest where water actually escapes, subject to service-head, switching and resilience constraints. Results are reported network by network rather than pooled alone. The pooled F1 reaches 0.916 and the Top-5 hit rate 0.816, against 0.836 and 0.573 for the strongest baseline, with per-network F1 ranging from 0.903 on C-Town to 0.932 on Net3 and mean detection latency falling to roughly four hours. On the official BattLeDIM 2019 scenarios, held out as an independent validation set, the same model retains an F1 of 0.818 but sheds about twenty points of Top-5 hit rate, which bounds how far the in-house training distribution generalizes. Closing the loop on C-Town raises leakage reduction from 24.6% under uniform depressurization to 37.5% while holding service compliance at 99.4%. Ablations identify state assimilation as the load-bearing component. Code and result records accompany the paper; scalability beyond a few thousand nodes, transient hydraulics and the capital cost of dense instrumentation remain open limitations.

papers.title: Emerging trends in AI-driven mining hazard management
papers.abstract: The management of geotechnical hazards in mining is critical for ensuring operational safety and sustainability, yet its practical implementation often struggles with the inherent geological uncertainty and the dynamic, non-linear nature of mining environments. Artificial intelligence (AI), and specifically machine learning (ML), has emerged as a transformative technology, offering a shift from reactive to proactive, data-driven hazard management. This paper provides a comprehensive review of the evolution and application of AI in mining hazard management, tracing this development from early statistical and ML models to recent advances in deep learning. The review finds that these advanced models have demonstrated significant success in tasks such as rockburst prediction, slope stability analysis, and gas outburst forecasting by identifying complex patterns in large, multi-source datasets from seismic, geological, and operational monitoring. Despite these successes, significant challenges persist: the efficacy of purely data-driven models is often limited by data scarcity, imbalanced datasets, and a lack of physical consistency; the black-box nature of many deep learning models has created a barrier to their interpretability and trustworthiness in safety-critical applications. The future of AI in mining hazard management lies not in isolated algorithms but in integrated, hybrid systems. Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) and explainable AI (XAI) are identified as critical frontiers. These approaches promise to create models that are not only more accurate and generalisable but also transparent and interpretable to engineering practitioners, bridging the gap between AI's theoretical potential and its practical application in creating safer mining environments.

papers.title: ¿Aumenta la exposición prenatal al paracetamol el riesgo de trastorno del espectro autista y trastorno por déficit de atención con hiperactividad? Una revisión paraguas y un meta‐meta‐análisis
papers.abstract: Resumen Objetivo Evaluar si la exposición prenatal al paracetamol (acetaminofén) se asocia con un mayor riesgo de trastorno del espectro autista (TEA) y trastorno por déficit de atención con hiperactividad (TDAH) en la descendencia, mediante un enfoque de meta‐meta‐análisis (umbrella review o revisión paraguas). Método Se realizó una revisión paraguas registrada (PROSPERO CRD420251243790) de revisiones sistemáticas con metaanálisis que evaluaban la exposición prenatal al paracetamol y el riesgo de TEA o TDAH. Las búsquedas se llevaron a cabo en seis bases de datos principales hasta noviembre de 2025. La calidad metodológica se evaluó mediante la herramienta AMSTAR‐2 y el solapamiento de los estudios primarios se cuantificó utilizando el área cubierta corregida ( corrected covered area , CCA). Se realizaron meta‐meta‐análisis de efectos aleatorios para modelos sin restricciones, modelos parcialmente restringidos por calidad y modelos completamente restringidos por calidad. Cuando el solapamiento fue elevado, se llevaron a cabo metaanálisis adicionales de estudios primarios con bajo riesgo de sesgo, cuyo riesgo de sesgo se evaluó mediante la herramienta ROBINS‐E. Resultados Se incluyeron siete metaanálisis, que comprendían más de tres millones de participantes. Los meta‐meta‐análisis sin restricciones mostraron asociaciones positivas de pequeña magnitud entre la exposición prenatal al paracetamol y tanto el TEA (RR = 1,17) como el TDAH (RR = 1,29). Sin embargo, al restringir los análisis a metaanálisis de mayor calidad y a estudios primarios con bajo riesgo de sesgo, las estimaciones del efecto se atenuaron de forma considerable y, en varios modelos, se aproximaron a la ausencia de asociación. Se observó una elevada heterogeneidad y un solapamiento sustancial, especialmente en los análisis de estudios primarios. Interpretación Las asociaciones observadas entre la exposición prenatal al paracetamol y los trastornos del neurodesarrollo probablemente están influenciadas por limitaciones metodológicas, entre ellas la confusión residual y la clasificación errónea de la exposición. La evidencia epidemiológica disponible en la actualidad no respalda una relación causal sólida, y el paracetamol continúa siendo un tratamiento de primera elección apropiado durante el embarazo cuando está clínicamente indicado.

papers.title: Combustion Separation Enables Repeated Recycling of Carbon Nanotubes from Ultra-lightweight Materials: Implications for Sound-Absorbing Applications
papers.abstract: Abstract Carbon nanotubes (CNTs) are costly and energy-intensive to manufacture, making their recovery from single-use ultra-lightweight materials (ULMs) important for sustainable carbon-resource recycling. We show that solvent-free combustion separation, which exploits the thermal-stability difference between CNTs and a cellulose nanofiber matrix, enables CNT recovery over three successive fabrication−combustion−recovery cycles. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, Raman spectroscopy, and thermogravimetric analysis show that CNT crystallinity is largely preserved despite progressive sodium impurity accumulation and reduced thermal stability. Critically, sound-absorbing ULMs fabricated from the recycled CNTs retain acoustic performance equivalent to that of pristine CNTs, confirming the practical viability of this recycling route.

papers.title: Bioprospecting perchlorate-reducing bacteria: report of the genera Psychrobacter, Planococcus, Carnobacterium, and Paeniglutamicibacter isolated in Cierva Point, Antarctica, and its contribution to SDG 3
papers.abstract: Abstract Perchlorate (ClO 4 − ) is a global contaminant that has been detected in various environmental matrices. ClO 4 − is considered an emerging pollutant because of its potent endocrine-disrupting effects, which impairs iodine uptake in the thyroid gland, and its high toxicity and persistence. Therefore, the development of technologies for its reduction in ecosystems is imperative; bioremediation is a promising technology for ClO 4 − reduction. In this study, bacterial strains isolated from marine sediments at Cierva Point, an Antarctic Specially Protected Area (ASPA No. 134), were characterized. The methodology consisted of four stages: i) isolation of the bacterial strains; ii) characterization of isolated strains by morphological, biochemical, and molecular traits; iii) susceptibility tests against NaCl and ClO 4 − ; iv) ClO 4 − removal assays using a selective electrode. The strains grew at 10 °C for 7 days and tolerated NaCl concentrations up to 30% w/v. All isolates grew at ClO 4 − concentrations of 10,000 mg/L, and five isolates also grew at 15,000 mg/L. Phylogenetic analysis identified members of the genera Psychrobacter, Planococcus, Carnobacterium , and Paeniglutamicibacter , capable of removing the contaminant in percentages between 40% and 52%. In alignment with UN Sustainable Development Goal 3 on promoting health and well-being, this project supports both ecosystem conservation and public health protection. In conclusion, the bacterial strains isolated from Cierva Point marine sediments, Antarctica, represent valuable resources for the bioremediation of ClO 4 − contamination, demonstrating significant potential to reduce and mitigate the pollutant in affected ecosystems.

papers.title: Synergistic effects of fibrolytic enzymes and lactic acid bacteria on cassava leaf silage quality and microbial community
papers.abstract: Cassava leaves are a valuable protein-rich feed resource, but their high fiber content and poor fermentation characteristics can reduce silage quality. To address these challenges, this study evaluated the synergistic effects of fiber-degrading enzymes and lactic acid bacteria (LAB) on the fermentation profiles, nutritional quality, and microbial community of cassava leaf silage. Silage was prepared using five treatments: CK (2% glucose), T1 (Lactobacillus plantarum + 2% glucose), T2 (glucanase + L. plantarum + 2% glucose), T3 (cellulase + L. plantarum + 2% glucose), and T4 (glucanase + cellulase + L. plantarum + 2% glucose), and ensiled for 0, 21, and 42 days. The findings demonstrated that additive treatments (T1-T4) rapidly decreased silage pH and increased lactic acid compared to the CK (P < 0.001). By day 42, the enzyme-inoculated groups (T2-T4) exhibited elevated crude protein alongside reduced fiber fractions compared to both CK and T1 (P < 0.001). Regarding the microbial community, Shannon and Simpson indices were lower in treated groups than in the CK group (P < 0.05). Beta diversity analysis revealed that the microbial community structure of the CK differed clearly from that of the additive-treated silages. At the phylum level, Bacillota dominated all other groups on day 42, with a relative abundance exceeding 92%. At the species level, Lactobacillus plantarum dominated enzyme-treated silages (relative abundance > 93%, P = 0.036), compared to only 13.1% in CK, which contained higher proportions of Pediococcus and Weissella species. Collectively, the synergistic application of fibrolytic enzymes and LAB improves cassava leaf silage quality by accelerating acidification, reducing fiber fractions, and establishing a highly favorable L. plantarum-dominated microbial community.

papers.title: Floating 3D‐Printed Grids: New Approach for Photocatalytic Degradation of Contaminants Under Direct Solar Radiation
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Water contamination by antibiotics and other emerging contaminants is ubiquitous across all water matrices worldwide, and underlines the need for sustainable, easy‐to‐deploy materials that operate efficiently in real aquatic environments. A straightforward implementation is essential for bridging laboratory developments to diverse practical water‐treatment scenarios. In this work, floating poly(vinylidene fluoride‐co‐hexafluoropropylene) (PVDF‐HFP) grids incorporating TiO 2 were fabricated via direct ink writing (DIW) 3D printing combined with salt leaching, thereby enabling precise control over geometry and porosity while overcoming the structural limitations of conventional techniques. The resulting grids exhibited interconnected porosity, strong mechanical stability, remarkable reusability, and effective photocatalytic performance, achieving 60% degradation of ciprofloxacin in 540 min under UV‐A radiation and complete degradation in about 120 min under natural sunlight. Distinctively, the materials maintained their photocatalytic activity across multiple reuse cycles, demonstrating robustness and operational durability. These results highlight the potential of this 3D‐printed floating system to provide a scalable, customisable and practical solution for water remediation using just sunlight.

papers.title: A Novel Application of the Volumetric Absorptive Micro Sampling Strategy to Quantify Dexmedetomidine in Capillary Blood Using an LC – MS / MS Method
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pain control in neonates is crucial as inadequate management may impair neuronal development. Dexmedetomidine (DEX), an alpha2 agonist, is approved for intravenous use in ventilated neonates. While intranasal DEX is off-label in neonates and children, studies show its efficacy for magnetic resonance imaging sedation. Limited pharmacokinetic data exist for intranasal DEX in pre-term infants and neonates. This study aimed to develop an analytical method for DEX quantification in blood samples (20 μL) of complex patients collected with microsampling technique to enable future pharmacokinetic studies. METHODS: A liquid-liquid extraction from blood absorbed in microsampling devices (MITRA) and an LC-MS/MS method were developed and validated following EMA/FDA guidelines. The method's suitability was verified by comparing results from nine paediatric blood samples collected in EDTA tubes or using MITRA devices. RESULTS: > 0.99), intra and inter-day repeatability (CV % 1.8-11.8), stability, and hematocrit effect met the acceptance criteria for bioanalytical method validation. Compared with plasma samples, the proposed method showed good consistency in detecting DEX in MITRA samples. CONCLUSION: The MITRA microsampling tools reduce the amount of blood needed and the risks of anemisation for neonates hospitalised and simplifies procedures, allowing a reduction of the staff involved in the routine. The analytical and clinical validation of the method demonstrated its suitability to quantify DEX in a range of concentrations potentially useful for pharmacokinetic studies in paediatric patients for approval use and drug monitoring.

papers.title: Agro-Waste Upcycling in Wound Care: Development And Characterization of An Alkali-Treated Coconut Coir and Alginate Composite Gauze for Sustained Herbal Delivery
authors: Ashwini G. Narwade, Ashwini K. Bhusari, Snehal R. Suradkar
Vaishnavi V. Shende Vaishnavi A. Deshmukh
Dr. S. L. Khedekar Dr. R. H. Kale
papers.journal: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
papers.abstract: Chronic and acute wounds place a heavy burden on patients and health systems, and conventional woven cotton gauze, although inexpensive and widely used, can adhere to the wound bed, shed lint and allow desiccation. Modern moisture-retentive dressings solve many of these problems but are costly and often non-biodegradable. At the same time, coconut (Cocos nucifera L.) processing generates very large quantities of husk that are burned or discarded. Coir, the lignocellulosic fibre of the husk, is porous, absorbent and biodegradable, and its properties can be improved by alkali and oxidative (H2O2) treatment. Sodium alginate, a seaweed polysaccharide that gels by ionic exchange with calcium, can be coated on a fibre matrix to create a moist, non-adherent, exudate-managing surface and a reservoir for herbal actives such as turmeric (Curcuma longa),neem, aloe vera and Centella asiatica. This review summarizes wound-healing physiology, the types of dressings, the history and limitations of gauze, the potential of agro-waste coir, the role of alginate hydrogels, and the evidence for herbal wound therapies. It then outlines a plan for developing and characterizing an alkali-treated coconut coir and alginate composite gauze for sustained herbal delivery, and identifies gaps that future work must address.
papers.summary: Chronic and acute wounds place a heavy burden on patients and health systems, and conventional woven cotton gauze, although inexpensive and widely used, can adhere to the wound bed, shed lint and allow desiccation. This review summarizes wound-healing physiology, the types of dressings, the history and limitations of gauze, the potential of agro-waste coir, the role of alginate hydrogels, and the evidence for herbal wound therapies. It then outlines a plan for developing and characterizing an alkali-treated coconut coir and alginate composite gauze for sustained herbal delivery, and identifies gaps that future work must address.

papers.title: Spatial and Spectral Decoupled Meta‐Window for Thermal Camouflage and Infrared Communication
papers.abstract: Thermal radiation carries energy and information, making simultaneous control of its spectral profile and spatial propagation crucial for infrared camouflage, signaling, and communication. However, most thermal materials prioritize spectral manipulation, leaving the propagation direction of broadband thermal signals underexplored and tightly coupled to the spectral response. Here, a spatial and spectral decoupled meta-window (SSDW) is demonstrated for independent control of the spectral profile and spatial distribution of broadband thermal radiation across 8-13 µm. By assigning directional reflection splitting and spectral tailoring to distinct geometric degrees of freedom, the SSDW exhibits visible haze, mid-infrared semitransparency, and broadband suppression of specular reflection, including at 10.6 µm. It maintains a stable apparent thermal signature both without external heat interference and under variations in external-source temperature, source incidence angle, and camera viewing angle. This enables visible-laser-infrared compatible camouflage, while preserving an outward channel for emergency signaling. As a proof-of-concept, the SSDW encodes the incidence direction of a 10.6 µm laser into spatial reflection patterns for assistive infrared communication, enabling reliable decoding over moderate angular variations. This work establishes spatial and spectral decoupling as a framework for thermal radiation engineering, extending control beyond radiative intensity toward coordinated heat and information pathways.

papers.title: Structural compatibility between β‐lactams and substrate binding pockets of IMP ‐1 and NDM ‐1 determines the substrate spectrum
papers.journal: Bulletin of the Korean Chemical Society
papers.abstract: Abstract The global spread of infectious diseases is exacerbated by rising antimicrobial resistance, with Metallo‐β‐lactamases (MBLs) contributing significantly by inactivating β‐lactam antibiotics. The enzyme's substrate spectrum is usually determined by structural compatibility between the substrate‐binding pocket (SBP) and the substrate. We studied the structural compatibility between the SBPs of IMP‐1 and NDM‐1 and six β‐lactam substrates, and the correlation between compatibility and hydrolytic activity. MBLs have a conserved SBP surrounded by three external loops. The SBP contains catalytic zinc‐binding sites at the center and R α and R β pockets on both sides. IMP‐1 has narrower R α and wider‐open R β pockets, while NDM‐1 has broader R α and less‐open R β pockets. Different classes of β‐lactams show distinct structural characteristics in the core rings and both side chains. We performed enzyme kinetics and molecular docking studies. Results show that higher structural compatibility, especially in the tighter R α pocket, is important for hydrolytic activity. The structural compatibility study will help clarify the substrate‐spectrum profile of MBLs across diverse β‐lactams.
